content:
I've built a formalization of the Hardy-Littlewood prime k-tuple conjecture with Claude based on Residual Number Systems and the Chinese Remainder theorem.

Code here: https://gist.github.com/golfbum71/63cf8ea8422f0d37596f34b984fe6b8d
(2400 lines ... with a lot of commented out lines trying to explain things)

I asked Grok to look at the code after it was done for a "second opinion." The bottom line is that it is different enough and polished enough to be worth extracting and contributing.

What is there is not a proof of the conjecture.

There is a Google's DeepMind statement-only lean formalization file, but Grok feels my supporting theory is "substantially richer and could improve or extend those entries."

I think what I've done isn't necessarily new ... but the way it is framed is different. I've constantly come against statements from the AI that what I've done isn't new ... it's just reframed it in a new way. I'm hoping that new way of looking at these problems might help others to move forward.

I would appreciate if anyone could take a look, verify if it is of any use, and if so, help make it better.

Cheers,
Geoff

Very unlikely that anyone will take a look without at least a Lean repository, using #comparator and #formalization.yaml. It's just the nature of things today: the default assumption is (reasonably!) that you've produced some AI slop. (And I say this as one of the most AI-enthustiastic people around here. :-)

Also, sycophantic quotes from Grok reduce anyone's interest, rather than increase it, I think...

Thanks for your reply. It’s basically my first post. I’m trying to learn a lot of new subjects. I will research the requirements you spelled out and see if I can get them correct. I also am working on revising the code … I had a lot of extra stuff in there.

Appreciate your thoughts and time.

Cheers!

@Kim Morrison ,
I'm hoping this is moving in the right direction:
https://github.com/golfbum71/HardyLittlewood

I'm working to get a repository for the comparator process...with a challenge file, etc.

The formalization.yaml ... I don't know what to say ... it has a lot of requirements I won't know the answer to. Regarding the people who helped/influenced? Who knows ... everyone ... I've watched hundreds of YouTube videos on the primes ... I might have taken something from all of them. And there are other items that are marked as required that someone who is brand new to this process would never know what is right or wrong to put.

I also don't have a linux machine to do the #comparator ... if that is needed. So much is unsaid. And if I missed the directions on how to write a good request for help...I apologize.

As far as mentioning Grok ... what can I say ... the reason I am here is because the AI models are the only ones who will "talk" with me. And I'm sure that most would appreciate that the AI is taking all my stupid questions rather than actual people.

I do feel like all the questions have lead somewhere as far as ideas are concerned. Lean was a way to verify if any of them panned out and were true. It was very cool that all the code checked out on the https://live.lean-lang.org/ site.

So ... that leads me to here...moving from talking to AI to bringing that work to those that might be able to use it.

Please believe me when I say that I appreciate your time. And I hope you are having a wonderful day!

Cheers,
Geoff

All,

Just curious ... instead of me creating a challenge file for the prime k-tuples conjecture. Is there anyone will to create a true challenge?

I've had to ask AI to make one ... then we're working on a bridge to map what I have to the challenge we created. That doesn't seem right.

If anyone were willing to set me against a true challenge ... I would appreciate it. In case it matters, the code I have is for the formalization of the problem, not the proof. That will be left alone.

If that's how it is supposed to be done.

Appreciate any help.

Cheers,
Geoff
